    Estimate child mortality with the Brass indirect method

    childmort_brass.Rd

    Estimate probabilities of dying in childhood from children ever born and children dead reported by women by age group. The function applies either the Trussell or Palloni-Helligman multipliers, locates each estimate in time, and interpolates the matching model life table level. Based on Manual X (UN, 1984)

    childmort_brass(
  CEB,
  CS = NULL,
  CD = NULL,
  W = 1,
  variant = NULL,
  mlt_model = NULL,
  Sex = NULL,
  date_obs = 0,
  age = seq(15, 45, 5),
  mam = NULL
)

    Arguments

    CEB

    Numeric vector. Children ever born by women's age group. Can be a mean.

    CS

    Numeric vector. Children alive by women's age group. Can be a mean.

    CD

    Numeric vector. Children dead by women's age group. Can be a mean.

    W

    Numeric vector. Women by age group. By Dfault is one, allowing mean numbers in CEB, CD or CS.

    variant

    Character. Multiplier variant to use. Options are "trussell" and "palloni_helligman". If NULL return both.

    mlt_model

    Character. Model life table family. If NULL return all. For "trussell", use one of "North", "South", "East", or "West". For "palloni_helligman", use one of "Latin", "Chilean", "South_Asian", "Far_East_Asian", or "General". If NULL, "West" is assumed. Some combinations of mlt_model and variant are not possible.

    Sex

    Character. Optional filter for "male", "female", or "both". If NULL, all three are returned. Both-sex model life tables use a sex ratio at birth of 1.04 males per female.

    date_obs

    Numeric decimal year, Date, or unambiguous character string in the format "YYYY-MM-DD". Reference date of the census or survey, converted to a decimal year to compute date_t, the time location of each estimate.

    age

    Numeric vector. Lower bounds of women's five-year age groups. This is a formality to keep the age reference to the user. The ages seq(15, 45, 5) are always expected.

    mam

    Numeric. Mean age at maternity. Used only with variant = "palloni_helligman". If NULL, 27 is assumed.

    Value

    A list with three data frames and a plot:

    table_output

    Summary by women's age group, variant, model life table family, sex, and reference date date_t. Includes infant mortality q0, the probability of dying between ages 1 and 5 q1_4, under-five mortality q0_5, and life expectancy at birth e0.

    plot_output

    A ggplot of q0 against by date, with a series for each variant and model life table family and panels by sex.

    qx_estimate

    Results for applying the coefficients, before finding the best MLT level.

    mlts_interp

    Interpolated model life table rows matched to each estimate. The elementtable_output is a summary of this.

    References

    United Nations. 1983. Manual X: Indirect Techniques for Demographic Estimation. United Nations, New York.

    Examples

    if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Manual X - Panama 1976 (table 49)
panama <- data.frame(
  age = seq(15, 45, 5),
  W = c(2695, 2095, 1828, 1605, 1362, 1128, 930),
  CEB = c(278, 1380, 2395, 3097, 3444, 3274, 2682),
  CD = c(24, 77, 172, 236, 348, 394, 354))
panama_estimate <- childmort_brass(
  CEB = panama$CEB,
  CD = panama$CD,
  W = panama$W,
  age = panama$age,
  mlt_model = "West",
  Sex = "male",
  date_obs = 1976
)
manual_x_rr <- c(0.0952, 0.0580, 0.0707, 0.0757, 0.1021, 0.1201, 0.1308)
round(panama_estimate$qx_estimate$qx - manual_x_rr,3)

# Example from mortpack template qfive.mpl
mortpak_example <- childmort_brass(
  CEB = c(0.154, 1.129, 2.562, 4.008, 5.237, 5.956, 6.243),
  CS = c(0.138, 0.999, 2.240, 3.477, 4.432, 4.946, 5.013),
  age = seq(15, 45, 5),
  Sex = "both",mlt_model = "Latin",
  date_obs = 1974, mam = 26)
mortpak_example_results <- data.frame(
  t_mortpak = c(1973, 1971.9, 1970.3, 1968.2, 1965.8, 1962.9, 1959.4),
  q0_mortpak = c(
    0.105830924787535, 0.0975754471500075,
    0.0917687827207557, 0.0872981426626247, 0.092390952214435, 
    0.0931828302627686, 0.100965457016312))
cbind(
  mortpak_example$table_output |> 
    select(date_t, q0),
  mortpak_example_results) |> 
  mutate(
    dif_t = round(date_t - t_mortpak, 1),
    dif_e0 = round(q0 - q0_mortpak, 3))

# IUSSP - Malawi 2008 (https://demographicestimation.iussp.org/content/indirect-estimation-child-mortality)
iussp_malawi_2008 <- childmort_brass(
  CEB = c(180178, 1038556, 1613374, 1697566, 1553676, 1335242, 1128423), 
  CS = c(161541, 919584, 1398776, 1426516, 1266514, 1043357, 851048),
  W = c(635927, 678071, 566350, 405602, 298004, 221274, 174875),
  age = seq(15, 45, 5),
  mlt_model = "North",Sex = "both",
  date_obs = 2008.46, mam = 28.7
)
iussp_example_results <- data.frame(
  t_iussp = c(2007.42, 2006.03, 2004.03, 2001.66, 1999.02, 1996.24, 1993.35),
  q0_iussp = c(0.1063, 0.0918, 0.0912, 0.1004, 0.1089, 0.1203, 0.1232))
# some difference because IUSSP adjust intercept from logit rather than interpolate linearly levels
cbind(
  iussp_malawi_2008$table_output |> 
    select(date_t, q0),
  iussp_example_results) |> 
  mutate(
    dif_t = round(date_t - t_iussp, 1),
    dif_q0 = round(q0 - q0_iussp, 3))
} # }
